extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reading and reasoning about text in images to answer. Questions are collected from images in the Open Images dataset from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard).
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were selected from Open Images v3 dataset from categories that tend to contain text. A three-stage pipeline was used: (1) annotators identified images containing text, (2) annotators provided 1-2 questions requiring reading text in the image, and (3) 10 answers were collected for each question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from Open Images v3 dataset, specifically from categories that tend to contain text such as billboard, traffic sign, and whiteboard.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered to remove those without text. Questions were filtered based on quality flags including: no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, and unanswerable. Bad annotators were identified and filtered using hand-crafted questions with known correct answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were shown images and asked to provide questions requiring reading text in the image. For the second question, annotators were shown the first question and asked to provide a different question with a different answer. 10 answers were collected for each question from different annotators. Instructions similar to VQA and VizWiz datasets were provided.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Questions were asked by sighted humans
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system was used to detect and extract text from images
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses an important problem for visually impaired users. Studies show that up to 21% of questions asked by visually impaired users involve reading and reasoning about text in images of their surroundings.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Question only baseline achieves 8.09% and Image only baseline achieves 6.29% validation accuracy, showing that the dataset does not have significant biases with respect to images and questions. The most common answer 'yes' is the majority answer for only 4.71% of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCR model fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., a scribble) or partially occluded. 8.9% of questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which is left as future work. In some cases where the OCR system is unable to detect text, 0 tokens are returned (restricted to 1.5k images).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and evaluating VQA models that can read and reason about text in images. It is split into train (34,602), validation (5,000), and test (5,734) sets. The dataset is well-suited to benchmark progress along directions complementary to VQA 2.0.

name.evidence: To this end, we introduce the TextVQA dataset.

description.evidence: TextVQA contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer.

url.evidence: To study the task of answering questions that require reading text in images, we collect a new dataset called TextVQA which is publicly available at https://textvqa.org

creator.evidence: Amanpreet Singh1, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah1, Yu Jiang1, Xinlei Chen1, Dhruv Batra1,2, Devi Parikh1,2, Marcus Rohrbach1

inLanguage.evidence: We use pre-trained GloVe embeddings with a custom vocabulary (top77k question words in the VQA 2.0) for the question embedding

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data. In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text (using a forced-choice 'yes'/'no' flag). Filtering those (and noisy data from annotators) out resulted in 28,408 images, which form the basis of our TextVQA dataset. In the second stage, we collect 1-2 questions for each image... Following VQA [3, 10] and VizWiz [13] datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We use Open Images v3 dataset [27] as the source of our images... We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data. In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text... In the second stage, we collect 1-2 questions for each image.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We use Open Images v3 dataset [27] as the source of our images. In line with the goal of developing and studying VQA models that can reason about text, we are most interested in the images that contain text in them. Several categories in Open Images fit this criterion (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text (using a forced-choice 'yes'/'no' flag). Filtering those (and noisy data from annotators) out resulted in 28,408 images... To ensure answer quality, we gave annotators instructions similar to those used in [3, 13] when collecting the VQA and VizWiz datasets. In addition, to catch any poor quality data from earlier steps, we give annotators these four options: (i) no text in image; (ii) not a question; (iii) answering the question doesn't require reading any text in image; and (iv) unanswerable, e.g. questions involving speculation about the meaning of text. We remove the questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags. Additionally, we use hand-crafted questions for which we know the correct answers to identify and filter out bad annotators.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For the first question, we show annotators an image and ask them to provide a question which requires reading the text in the image to answer. Specifically, they were told to 'Please ensure that answering the question requires reading of the text in the image. It is OK if the answer cannot be directly copied from the text but needs to be inferred or paraphrased.' To collect a second question that is different from the first, we show annotators the first question and ask them to come up with a question that requires reasoning about the text in the image and has a different answer. Following VQA [3, 10] and VizWiz [13] datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question. To ensure answer quality, we gave annotators instructions similar to those used in [3, 13] when collecting the VQA and VizWiz datasets.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% questions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Following VQA [3, 10] and VizWiz [13] datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: It contains 45,336 questions asked by (sighted) humans on 28,408 images from the Open Images dataset

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: For OCR, we run the Rosetta OCR system [6] to provide us word strings s1; :::; sN.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: the VizWiz study [5] found that up to 21% of these questions involve reading and reasoning about the text captured in the images of a user's surroundings – 'what temperature is my oven set to?', 'what denomination is this bill?'. ... Models that do well on this dataset will not only need to parse the image and the question as in traditional VQA, but also read the text in the image, identify which of the text might be relevant to the question, and recognize whether a subset of the detected text can directly be the answer (e.g., in the case of 'what temperature is my oven set to?') or additional reasoning is required on the detected text to answer the question (e.g., 'which team is winning?').

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Question only (Q) and Image only (I) baseline get 8.09% and 6.29% validation accuracies, respectively, which shows that the dataset does not have significant biases w.r.t. images and questions... The most common answer ('yes') is the majority answer for only 4.71% of the dataset

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Our OCR model, while mature, still fails at detecting text that is rotated, a bit unstructured (e.g., a scribble) or partially occluded... 8.9% of the TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens; we leave this as future work... In some cases, when the system is unable to detect text we get 0 tokens but those cases are restricted to 1.5k images and we manually verified that the images actually do contain text.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We divide TextVQA into train, validation and test splits with size 34,602, 5,000, and 5,734, respectively. The TextVQA questions collected from Open Images v3's training set were randomly split into training and validation sets. There is no image overlap between the sets... We find that the gap between human performance and machine performance is significantly larger on TextVQA than on VQA 2.0, suggesting that TextVQA is well-suited to benchmark progress along directions complementary to VQA 2.0.
